title: Individual message versus structural cue
rationale: Only the Perception gap video lowered affective polarization (-2.3, 95% CI [-4.3, -0.4], n=641) among 32 arms, and the study cannot test structural causes. This 2x2 crosses the video with a hostile elite/media feed prime to see whether the individual-level correction survives a hostile environment.
contribution: Directly tests whether an individual-level perception correction is overridden by structural hostility cues rather than assuming either account.
limitations: A brief feed prime is a weak proxy for a sustained media environment.
Prime precedes the video, so order effects are untested.
Outcomes are measured immediately; durability is unknown.
Interaction power is limited unless the target n is reached.

design.title: Perception gap video x hostile versus neutral feed prime
design.overview: US adults first see a feed of either hostile elite and media content or neutral content. They then see the Perception gap video or a control screen. Then affective polarization and support for undemocratic practices are measured.
design.hypothesis: If individual interventions have leverage, the video lowers affective polarization under both primes. If the structural account holds, the video effect shrinks or vanishes under the hostile prime (video x prime interaction > 0).
design.primaryOutcome: Affective polarization: in-party minus out-party feeling thermometer.
design.comparison: Video vs control within each prime; the video x prime interaction contrast; secondary outcome is support for undemocratic practices.
design.population: US adults from an online panel, with party identification (including leaners) collected; pure independents screened out.

questions.text: You are invited to a research study on political attitudes. It takes about 10 minutes, is voluntary, and responses are anonymous. Do you consent to participate?
Do you think of yourself as closer to the Republican Party or to the Democratic Party?
Please read this set of posts from a news feed: local weather forecasts, a new library opening, a recipe feature, and a sports score recap. {{ed:feed_neutral}}
Please read this set of posts from a news feed: politicians and commentators attacking the other party as dangerous and corrupt, and headlines about escalating partisan conflict. {{ed:feed_hostile}}

Please rate each group on a feeling thermometer from 0 to 100. Ratings of 50 to 100 mean you feel favorable and warm; ratings of 0 to 50 mean you do not feel favorable; 50 means neither warm nor cold.
Please indicate your agreement and disagreement with the following statements.

rows.text: My party should reduce the number of polling stations in areas that support the other party.
Governors of my party should ignore unfavorable court rulings by judges appointed by the other party.
Governors of my party should prosecute journalists who accuse my party's politicians of misconduct without revealing sources.
Members of my party should not accept the results of elections if they lose.

questions.text: What did you just see, read, or watch?

Thank you. This study examined how political information affects attitudes. The news feed posts were selected examples, and the video presented survey data on how people view the other party. Thank you for participating.

assumptions: Power: about 800 per arm (about 3,200 total) to detect an interaction of 2.0 thermometer points at 80% power, since the observed main effect of -2.3 (SE 1.0, n=641) implies roughly 800 per cell.
Online panel of US partisans and leaners; pre-treatment thermometer is not collected, to keep the survey short; covariates are adjusted via party.
Thermometer is collected as banded Matrix categories because only MC/TE/DB/Matrix types are allowed; the platform may substitute the original slider.
Analysis: OLS with HC2 errors, video x prime interaction, two-sided.
unresolved: Actual feed screenshots and the Perception gap video file must be supplied by the research team.
IRB approval number and compensation must be supplied.
